title: EA producer confirms the return of Wing Commander

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A panel at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo on game preservation revealed that the master tapes containing high quality source video for Wing Commander III were located.
The contents of these tapes will now undergo restoration and preparation is at work for a new release of the game, tentatively called Wing Commander III 30th Anniversary Edition.
For a certain generation of gamers, somewhere above the age of 30, this is big news. Wing Commander III, subtitled ‘The Heart of the Tiger’ launched way back in 1994.

It was one of the first and most successful games to incorporate full motion video cutscenes alongside its polygonal 3D combat. For these sequences, developer Origin Systems enlisted Hollywood actors such as Mark Hamill, Malcolm McDowell and John Rhys-Davies.

blocks.caption: Wing Commander III stars Ginger Lynn Allen, Mark Hamill and Jennifer MacDonald via Wing Commander CIC

blocks.text: It was all part of a broader trend – one I refer to as ‘the multimedia era’ – in video gaming to flex the storage capacity of CD-ROMs and the growing audiovisual muscle of desktop PC hardware.

This was before specialized 3D hardware became commonplace, so the answer to that was frequently big production values comparable to Hollywood movies, a medium that video games continue to emulate to this day, for better or worse.
Many of these attempts are now historical curiosities at best, willfully forgotten mistakes at worst.
For every The Beast Within: A Gabriel Knight Mystery there is a Psychic Detective and for every The 7th Guest there was a Tender Loving Care.
Today, games like Alan Wake 2 and Immortality are better at incorporating live action performances, making artistic use of them rather than as storytelling crutches.

The challenge of 30 year old technologies and file formats
Jim Vessella, the senior producer at EA, who hosted the panel, said that the remaster of Wing Commander III will involve brushing off video compression.
He also mentioned features such as “Kilrathi Saga Integration,” and the inclusion of community enhancement patches.
Attendees report that the uncompressed original footage is set to ship with the upscaled version, with a toggle allowing players to switch between them.

blocks.caption: EA senior producer Jim Vessella at Portland Retro Gaming Expo via Wing Commander CIC

blocks.text: Wing Commander III was originally shot on tape with the footage being reduced to 320×240 videos and encoded in an obscure but primitive format known as ‘Xanmovie.’
By comparison, the sequels Wing Commander IV and Wing Commander Prophecy were shot on 35mm film and eventually received limited releases as DVD games with slightly better compression.
The masters for Wing Commander III were believed lost when EA closed Origin in 2004.
Vessella was a producer on this year’s Star Wars: Zero Company, and he also helped lead the charge on a similar remaster, 2020’s Command & Conquer: Remastered Collection.
Vessella’s panel at the Portland Retrogaming Expo has him listed not just as a producer, but as a “driving force in Electronic Arts’ game preservation effort.”
This role has allowed for the digitization of archival assets and the release of source code for classic titles.
